records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1, a rental box van with a gross vehicle weight of 14,500 lbs., was traveling north bound at 14834 north freeway and turned into a gas station parking lot and was then traveling south through said parking lot. as unit 1 approached the center gas pump station, pumps 7 and 8, unit 1 turned left (east) around pump 7 where the pedestrian was standing nearby sweeping and possibly ran over the pedestrians right foot causing minor injuries. the driver of unit 1 reported he was several feet away from the pedestrian as he turned and never struck the pedestrian. the two passengers inside unit 1 reported no contact was made with the pedestrian due to her facing south with a broom and dust pan in her hands which was between her and unit 1 and could not have ran her over without also striking the broom and dust pan. the pedestrian reported she was standing a few feet away from pump 7 sweeping up debris as unit 1 turned the corner at pump 7 and ran over her foot causing her to fall to the ground. i inspected unit 1 and found the rear left wheel assembly about 12 to 15 inches under the body of the truck. this would have required the pedestrians foot to be extended out in front of her in order to be hit by unit 1's rear wheel. i inspected the pedestrians right shoe, a blue colored thin and light mesh material tennis shoe, and saw no indication her foot was ran over; no tire marks, impressions or damage was seen. i met and identified the on-duty store manager of stripes, linda kirkwood, (281) 209-7709, who allowed me to review the footage of the incident from the security camera system. while viewing the incident, visibility was poor with dark shadows distorting the view. but, from a distance the pedestrian can be seen a few feet away from unit 1 as the vehicle made the turned around pump 7. the pedestrian can be seen falling to the ground as unit 1 passes. due to the angle of the camera it was not possible to see any contact made between unit 1 and the pedestrian. harris county emergency corp medic 95 transported [medical facility] for evaluation. in order to determine if the pedestrian sustained injuries medical records will have to be obtained. end report.

records.deidentified_narrative: [roadway], [roadway], divided, marked roadway with three lanes going north and three lanes going south. driver of unit 1 stated that he was traveling south bound [roadway]. driver of unit 1 stated that as he was traveling south, he observed a female running east to west from the center median across the roadway without using a crosswalk. driver of unit 1 stated that this distracted him and made him look as the female ran across. driver of unit 1 stated that as he was distracted he felt and heard a hard impact to the front of his vehicle. the pedestrian was on a scooter going from east to west from the center median across the roadway without using a crosswalk. driver of unit 1 stated that he did not know what he hit and continued driving. driver of unit 1 stated that as he drove he saw people running to where he felt the impact. driver of unit 1 stated that he stopped at a parking lot (1 block away, 9757 dyer) to look at the damage to his vehicle. driver of unit 1 stated that he then walked towards where the impact occurred and that was when he saw the body of the pedestrian laying on the roadway without signs of life. officers located a witness who stated that he only heard the impact but did not observe it. jehu delgado, (915)881-7056. officer e. nevarez #2648 (sti #17) of the el paso police department-special traffic investigations unit was assigned this report for further investigation. based on the investigation of this case, it is believed that the pedestrian was in the process of crossing across the southbound lanes of the 9800 block of dyer in an east to west direction riding a kick scooter, not at a crosswalk, when he was struck by unit #1. after striking the pedestrian, unit #1 continued to travel south on dyer without stopping. driver of unit #1 drove the vehicle to a nearby restaurant parking lot located at 9757 dyer (tejas cafe). after assessing the vehicle damage, driver of unit #1 returned to the collision site and identified himself as the operator and sole occupant of the vehicle at the time of this collision to a police officer on-scene. a reconstruction/speed analysis of this event determined that unit #1 speed at impact with the pedestrian was not a contributing factor in the causation of the collision. the pedestrians autopsy report-toxicology results showed him positive for delta-9 tch: 2. 3 ng/ml. this report was updated to reflect new findings of the investigation. further details can be found in related investigative report eppd [case id].

driver of unit 1 stated that as he was traveling south, he observed a female running east to west from the center median across the roadway without using a crosswalk. driver of unit 1 stated that this distracted him and made him look as the female ran across. driver of unit 1 stated that as he was distracted he felt and heard a hard impact to the front of his vehicle. the pedestrian was on a scooter going from east to west from the center median across the roadway without using a crosswalk. driver of unit 1 stated that he did not know what he hit and continued driving. driver of unit 1 stated that as he drove he saw people running to where he felt the impact. driver of unit 1 stated that he stopped at a parking lot (1 block away, 9757 dyer) to look at the damage to his vehicle. driver of unit 1 stated that he then walked towards where the impact occurred and that was when he saw the body of the pedestrian laying on the roadway without signs of life. officers located a witness who stated that he only heard the impact but did not observe it. jehu delgado, (915)881-7056. officer e. nevarez #2648 (sti #17) of the el paso police department-special traffic investigations unit was assigned this report for further investigation. based on the investigation of this case, it is believed that the pedestrian was in the process of crossing across the southbound lanes of the 9800 block of dyer in an east to west direction riding a kick scooter, not at a crosswalk, when he was struck by unit #1. after striking the pedestrian, unit #1 continued to travel south on dyer without stopping. driver of unit #1 drove the vehicle to a nearby restaurant parking lot located at 9757 dyer (tejas cafe). after assessing the vehicle damage, driver of unit #1 returned to the collision site and identified himself as the operator and sole occupant of the vehicle at the time of this collision to a police officer on-scene. a reconstruction/speed analysis of this event determined that unit #1 speed at impact with the pedestrian was not a contributing factor in the causation of the collision. the pedestrians autopsy report-toxicology results showed him positive for delta-9 tch: 2. 3 ng/ml. this report was updated to reflect new findings of the investigation. further details can be found in related investigative report eppd [case id].

records.deidentified_narrative: the [roadway] just west of the [roadway] is a four-lane farm to market roadway that has two marked e/b lanes and two marked w/b lanes separated by a double-yellow center divider. [roadway] is a highly congested business district with housing nearby. the roadway consists of gravel overlay and is in fair condition. visibility was good at the reported time of the collision. unit one was traveling w/[roadway] of the [roadway]. unit two was with three other siblings in the parking lot of the rancier food mart, located at [roadway]. unit two failed to yield the right of way to a vehicle and according to witnesses and physical evidence, ran into the roadway in front of unit one. due to unit two's center of gravity being below the leading edge of unit one, unit two was dragged underneath unit one until expelled out of the rear end. the perception-reaction distance was approximately 41' and post impact skid marks were measured at approximately 61'. published data for determining a conservative co-efficient of friction on this type of roadway is . 70. the post impact minimum speed formula indicates a speed of approximately 35 miles per hour. in addition, a vehicle impact with a pedestrian has negligible effects on the loss of speed therefore the speed determined is most likely the true speed at the time of impact. in addition, the perception-reaction distance supports the determined speed. at 35 miles per hour, unit one is traveling at 51fps. from the point of impact until the first evidence of braking being at 41', it supports unit one traveling at a reasonable speed as published data indicates an average 1. 5 second p/r time and if used in this situation would have been 76'. there was no physical evidence to support unit one to be traveling at an unreasonable speed, nor being distracted as his reaction time was more responsive than the commonly used 1. 5 second threshold. unit two sustained major injuries and was last reported to be critical but stable condition. several written witness statements were obtained and submitted.

[roadway] is a highly congested business district with housing nearby. the roadway consists of gravel overlay and is in fair condition. visibility was good at the reported time of the collision. unit one was traveling w/[roadway] of the [roadway]. unit two was with three other siblings in the parking lot of the rancier food mart, located at [roadway]. unit two failed to yield the right of way to a vehicle and according to witnesses and physical evidence, ran into the roadway in front of unit one. due to unit two's center of gravity being below the leading edge of unit one, unit two was dragged underneath unit one until expelled out of the rear end. the perception-reaction distance was approximately 41' and post impact skid marks were measured at approximately 61'. published data for determining a conservative co-efficient of friction on this type of roadway is . 70. the post impact minimum speed formula indicates a speed of approximately 35 miles per hour. in addition, a vehicle impact with a pedestrian has negligible effects on the loss of speed therefore the speed determined is most likely the true speed at the time of impact. in addition, the perception-reaction distance supports the determined speed. at 35 miles per hour, unit one is traveling at 51fps. from the point of impact until the first evidence of braking being at 41', it supports unit one traveling at a reasonable speed as published data indicates an average 1. 5 second p/r time and if used in this situation would have been 76'. there was no physical evidence to support unit one to be traveling at an unreasonable speed, nor being distracted as his reaction time was more responsive than the commonly used 1. 5 second threshold. unit two sustained major injuries and was last reported to be critical but stable condition. several written witness statements were obtained and submitted.
